title: Streaming edge cases scratchpad (SDK parity) — failure modes + required behavior
content:
Context / why I’m writing this
- We keep getting “stream drops behind proxy” + “timeouts ignored during streaming” + “works in TS but not in Python” reports.
- Goal: enumerate real failure modes and decide what the SDK standard MUST do vs what we only document.
- This is intentionally messy; will feed into: streaming quickstart + typed errors + conformance fixtures.

Assumptions
- Streaming is SSE (text/event-stream) over HTTP; client iterates events/chunks.
- Streaming retries are dangerous (duplicate tool calls / side effects / billing concerns) so default policy should be conservative.
- We still need consistent semantics across Python/TS/Go for:
  - when we throw vs when we return partial output
  - what error fields are available (request_id, status_code if any, retryable flag, disconnect_reason)
  - how timeouts behave (overall vs “idle/read timeout” during streaming)

Observed / plausible streaming failure modes (grouped)

A) Connection establishment / early termination (no tokens delivered)
1) DNS failure / TCP connect failure
- e.g., ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, i/o timeout
- Expected: retryable (as network error) per retry policy standard.
- SDK should preserve attempt_count + last_error.

2) TLS handshake error
- could be intermittent / proxy MITM / bad cipher
- Expected: treat as network error; retryable (bounded).

3) HTTP response arrives but is not streamable
- 401/403 auth errors
- 404 wrong path
- 413 payload too large
- 429 rate limited (should include Retry-After)
- 5xx gateway/server errors
- Expected:
  - Non-streaming-style error object (typed) before yielding any stream events.
  - Retry policy applies normally (429/408/409/5xx etc). For 429 respect Retry-After.

4) Server closes immediately after headers (FIN right away)
- Seen in some proxy timeouts; also happens when upstream worker dies right after accept.
- Expected: if no events delivered -> treat as retryable network/stream error (still effectively “pre-stream”).

B) Mid-stream disconnects (partial tokens delivered)
These are the tricky ones.

5) Server FIN mid-chunk / mid-event
- For SSE, client may have partial bytes not forming a complete event (e.g., got “data: {…partial json…”) then FIN.
- Risks:
  - client might silently drop the partial bytes and surface last complete event only
  - client might throw low-level parse error (JSON parse error) instead of “stream interrupted”
- Required behavior (proposal):
  - SDK MUST throw a typed StreamingInterruptedError (name TBD) when the stream ends unexpectedly.
  - Error MUST include: request_id (if known), received_event_count, received_bytes (best effort), and a disconnect_reason string.
  - SDK MUST NOT attempt automatic retry once any stream content has been yielded (default). (Document manual retry guidance w/ idempotency.)
  - SDK SHOULD preserve partial text accumulated so far (either on the exception as partial_output, or via a callback/event before throwing). Need consistent cross-language approach.

6) TCP RST (connection reset) mid-stream
- Often shows as ECONNRESET.
- Same expected semantics as #5.

7) HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) / GOAWAY
- Some environments use h2; proxies can send GOAWAY.
- Important: may not be distinguishable from generic “connection closed”.
- Required behavior: map into disconnect_reason like "http2_stream_reset" when detectable else "connection_closed".

8) Idle timeout enforced by intermediary (proxy / LB / NAT)
- Pattern: stream pauses (model stall, long tool call, or just slow generation). Proxy has idle timeout (often 60s / 120s). It kills connection.
- In practice: customer behind enterprise proxy complains “stream drops at ~60s”.
- Required behavior:
  - SDK streaming read timeout semantics should be “idle timeout between bytes/events”, not “total wall time” unless user sets overall timeout.
  - Standard should define default streaming idle timeout higher than non-streaming read timeout (or disable read timeout for streaming by default and rely on overall timeout). This is still an open question.
  - If we do have idle timeout and it triggers, error should be typed TimeoutError with timeout_scope="read_idle" (or equivalent).

9) Proxy buffering / delayed flush
- Proxy buffers chunks and releases in larger bursts. Client sees nothing for N seconds then gets a bunch.
- Failure mode: client-side idle timeout triggers even though server is producing (proxy is holding).
- Required behavior:
  - Same as #8: idle timeout must be configurable + clearly documented.
  - SDK should recommend increasing streaming idle timeout when behind proxies.

10) Proxy transforms stream / strips SSE headers
- Some proxies remove "Content-Type: text/event-stream" or buffer until completion.
- Expected: client might read entire response then parse as one event => bad UX.
- Required behavior:
  - If response content-type is not event-stream but user requested stream=true, SDK should error early with a clear message (misconfigured proxy / endpoint) OR fallback to non-streaming parse only if safe. I lean: error early (avoid confusing partial parse).

11) Corporate proxy / SSL inspection injecting HTML error page mid-stream
- Rare but nasty: body switches to HTML error with 200 or 502.
- Required behavior:
  - If we detect non-SSE framing mid-stream (e.g., parse fails), throw StreamingProtocolError with first N bytes sampled (redacted / truncated) for debugging.

12) Chunked encoding corruption
- “invalid chunk size” errors from some intermediaries.
- Required behavior: treat as stream protocol error; typed error; no auto-retry after partial output.

C) Client-side cancellation / backpressure
13) User cancels via AbortController / context cancel / closing iterator
- Expected: SDK should stop reading, close underlying response body, and not report as error (or throw a specific CancelledError).
- Required behavior:
  - Provide a distinct cancellation error type OR a clean termination signal.
  - Ensure request is actually aborted (avoid leaked connections).
  - Ensure we don’t classify cancellation as retryable.

14) Consumer stops reading without canceling (GC / forgotten iterator)
- Leads to open socket until server closes.
- Not much we can do; doc best practices.
- Might add finalizer warnings in some languages (maybe too much).

15) Slow consumer (backpressure)
- For SSE, if app can’t process quickly, buffers grow. Some clients will accumulate.
- Required behavior: try to stream incrementally, avoid unbounded buffering. Document that callbacks should be fast.

D) Server/application-level anomalies
16) Server sends malformed SSE event
- e.g., missing "data:" lines, invalid JSON within data payload, or multi-line data not handled consistently.
- Required behavior: StreamingProtocolError with event_index and a truncated raw event payload.

17) Server sends explicit error event then closes
- We might (now or future) emit an event that indicates error, or we might just terminate.
- Required behavior: if an error is provided in-band, SDK should convert to typed APIError and stop iteration.

18) Tool/function calling mid-stream and then disconnect
- If we’re streaming tool-call deltas, partial tool call arguments could exist.
- Required behavior:
  - SDK must not auto-invoke tools; it only surfaces tokens/events.
  - If disconnect mid-tool-call payload, error should include partial structured payload if possible (best effort) but no promises.

What should the STANDARD require? (rough draft)

1) No silent truncation
- If the stream ends unexpectedly, SDK MUST NOT just end iteration as if completed.
- Must throw a typed error unless the server explicitly indicates completion (e.g., terminal event).

2) “Pre-first-byte” vs “post-first-byte/token” retry line
- If no stream events have been yielded, treat as regular request failure:
  - apply standard retry policy (429/5xx/network), respect Retry-After.
- If at least one event/token has been delivered:
  - default: no automatic retry
  - provide docs: safe retry patterns require idempotency keys and application-level dedup.

3) Partial output handling
- Need cross-language consistency here.
- Options:
  A) Exception includes partial_output string + partial_events list (probably too heavy)
  B) SDK always yields events as they arrive; on error, caller keeps whatever it accumulated.
  C) Hybrid: yield events + include a “last_event” / “partial_text” field on error.
- My vote: B + minimal metadata on error. But Support wants “what was the last token?”; might be too much to standardize.
- Required at minimum: the SDK should never destroy already-yielded content.

4) Error taxonomy + fields for streaming errors
- Introduce StreamingInterruptedError (or StreamDisconnectedError) separate from generic APIError.
- Fields (cross-language canonical names; language idioms can differ but should map):
  - message
  - request_id (nullable if never received)
  - status_code (nullable; if we never got headers)
  - retryable (bool; for post-first-event default false)
  - retry_after_ms (nullable)
  - attempt (int) and max_attempts (int) if retry loop is in play
  - disconnect_reason (enum-ish string): connection_closed, connection_reset, read_timeout, http2_reset, protocol_error, proxy_interference, unknown
  - received_event_count (best effort)

5) Timeout semantics for streaming
- We need to decide how overall/connect/read map for streaming.
- For streaming, “read timeout” should behave as idle timeout between bytes/events, not total stream duration.
- Overall timeout should cap total wall time if user opts in.
- Cancellation should be immediate and consistent.

6) Request ID propagation
- If gateway provides request_id in headers early, SDK should capture it even if body parsing fails.
- If request_id shows up only in an error frame (non-stream), capture from body.

Test cases to add to conformance suite (notes)
- Fixture: stream that sends 2 events then closes socket abruptly (FIN) mid-third event.
  - Expect: 2 events delivered, then StreamingInterruptedError.
- Fixture: stream that stalls for > idle timeout then resumes.
  - Expect: if idle timeout < stall => TimeoutError; if idle timeout > stall => no error.
- Fixture: proxy-buffer simulation (no bytes for 30s then burst).
  - Validate idle timeout behavior.
- Fixture: non-event-stream content-type returned while stream requested.
  - Expect: clear error message.
- Fixture: 429 response w/ Retry-After returned for stream request (before any tokens).
  - Expect: SDK retries respecting Retry-After.

Open questions / TODOs
- What is the default streaming idle timeout? (Need SRE input; risk of hung connections vs premature drops.)
- Do we include partial_output on the thrown error across languages? If yes, define maximum size / truncation.
- Should we treat certain mid-stream failures as retryable if we can guarantee idempotency? (Probably no by default; document only.)
- Should SDK expose an explicit “stream completed” terminal signal (e.g., done event) vs relying on server semantics? (Depends on current API; check quickstart + gateway behavior.)

Notes from support / customer reports (paraphrased)
- SUP-29505: Enterprise proxy drops SSE connections; customers need guidance to tune timeouts and detect partial output.
- SUP-29410: Python streaming appears to ignore configured timeouts (likely timeout only applied to initial request, not the streaming read loop).

Next steps
- Turn this into a short section for the streaming guide: “Common disconnect causes + what to do”.
- Align naming of disconnect_reason across SDKs for logging/telemetry fields:
  - request_id, retry_count, timeout_ms, streaming_disconnect_reason.
- Feed into ENG-5125 (Go streaming reliability) + ENG-5127 (conformance fixtures).
